newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Dutch Queen Beatrix sees South African parliament.
newsitem.headline: Dutch Queen Beatrix sees South African parliament.

text.p: Queen Beatrix of the Netherlands, rounding off a four-day state visit to South Africa, on Thursday visited the Cape Town parliament in which apartheid was enacted and later dismantled.

Crown Prince Willem Alexander arrived from Johannesburg with his mother, but flew separately by helicopter to Robben Island in Table Bay, where President Nelson Mandela spent 18 of his 27 years in jail for fighting white rule.
The queen's visit was the first by a Dutch monarch to the country that was ruled for more than 45 years by a Calvinist white minority of Dutch-descended Afrikaners.
Frene Ginwala, speaker of the South African parliament, showed Beatrix the national assembly in which Mandela was elected as the country's first black president in 1994.

Cyril Ramaphosa, secretary general of the ruling African National Congress, showed her the former whites-only chamber in which apartheid was enacted and in which Dutch-born prime minister Hendrik Verwoerd was assassinated by a lone fanatic in 1966.
The queen's programme for the day included museum visits and, at her own request, a seminar with Afrikaans-language writers.

Her final appointment before a private holiday in the country was a scheduled meeting with the Dutch community in the 17th century castle built by Dutch seaman Jan van Riebeeck, South Africa's first European settler.
